summary: Verified the layered mismatch/low-confidence defense for AUREM CTO chat. Backend unit tests (4/4 test_response_confidence_mismatch_gate.py + 1/1 test_citation_guard_persist_ordering.py) all pass. Live preview /chat/send + /chat/stream + /chat/history plumbing confirmed via direct API calls with test@aurem.dev credentials. Simple prompts (What is 5+5?, hello, 2+2) return normal, correct, RELEVANT answers with low_confidence=false — mitigation is NOT over-blocking normal chat. Short codebase Q&A (who handles billing?) also gets a real answer, NOT the fallback (regression from unit-testing phase confirmed fixed). Legit bug-fix request also returns a real answer with low_confidence=false. UI e2e (Playwright) sent 'What is 5+5?', 'hello', '2+2' via ChatPanel — got normal responses ('5+5=10', 'Hey there!', 'Easy — it's 4') with zero low-confidence badges and zero fallback text; ORA council caption '5-adviser council · chairman verdict' rendered correctly (regression check #6 passed). Could not force the original mismatch bug in preview (as expected — main agent already tried 10x). Overall: mitigation implementation is verified working end-to-end and does NOT break normal chat.

critical_code_review_comments: response_confidence.py: is_definitional_mismatch() correctly excludes fix-intent AND code-signal messages before flagging — the earlier regression (file-path-only trigger) is confirmed removed.
chat.py: low_confidence flag is threaded consistently through both endpoints, both meta and done SSE frames, /chat/send JSON, and _persist_turn — clean end-to-end plumbing.
